Guidance & outlook: Looking ahead, given the strong start in Q1 , we are confident of delivering a clear step-up in our FY27 full year growth.
So, our ambition of 2x revenue from FY25 to FY30 and 3x EBITDA in the same period remains the North Star for us, and we remain confident of delivering that.
So, we expect filter growth to clock-in ahead of AMC growth, and therefore, between th em, we expect the 2x revenue to be tuned up.
Growth & demand: Revenue for the quarter grew by 15.3% year-on -year to INR701 crores, supported by accelerated and broad -based growth across the product business, especially water.
The water purifier category grew by high teens, on the back of a double -digit volume growth.
Service charges grew by 2.7% year-on -year to INR83 crores, reflecting the relatively softer growth in the underlying service bookings to some extent, and our ongoing initiatives to curb leakages.
Margins & costs: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 58.4%, lower by 131 basis points year-on-year, reflecting the impact of higher commodity costs and adverse currency movements.
While the cost environment remains challenging, and we are yet to see any meaningful reduction in input costs , our focus will be on driving our cost savings program and product mix.
As a result of the above, adjusted EBITDA for the quarter grew by 10.5% year- on-year to INR74 crores with adjusted EBITDA margins at 10.5%.

We expect operating leverage and cost efficiencies to kick in over a period of time, supported by productivity gains.
We ended the quarter with a net cash surplus of INR425 crores.
Risks & challenges: The operating landscape in Q1 continued to be impacted by inflationary pressures and currency volatility and the associated uncertainty.

Growth & demand: FY26 PERFORMANCE SUMMARY Despite a challenging macro environment for much of the year, the Company delivered revenue growth of 11.3% to ₹ 2,710 Crore, making FY26 our second consecutive year of double ‑digit growth.

Growth was broad ‑based, supported by strong momentum in manufacturing and services, alongside healthy expansion in private consumption and fixed capital formation, both of which grew by more than 7% during the year.
While growth is expected to moderate from the high base of FY26, IMF projects GDP growth of 6.5% in FY27.
Margins & costs: Adjusted EBITDA grew 16.4% to ₹ 332 Crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin improving by 55 basis points to 12.2%.
This marks our third consecutive year of margin expansion, with EBITDA margins improving from 6.3% in FY23 to 12.2% in FY26.
2x Revenue (FY25-30) 3x Adjusted EBITDA (FY25-30) We have set an aspiration to grow revenue to ₹ 5,400‑5,600 Crore and EBITDA to ₹ 800 ‑850 Crore by FY30 ‑double revenue and triple EBITDA from FY25.
Capex & expansion: In parallel, capital expenditure increased significantly from ₹ 11 Crore in FY23 to ₹ 84 Crore in FY26, reflecting the Company's focus on building scalable infrastructure and capabilities to support future growth.
Capex intensity increased from 0.5% of revenue in FY23 to 3.1% in FY26, underscoring the Company's commitment to investing ahead of the curve to drive long‑term growth.

The Company ended FY26 with a net cash surplus of ₹ 443 Crore, providing substantial financial flexibility to pursue growth opportunities, invest in innovation and customer experience, and navigate evolving market conditions.
Balance sheet & cash: Over the last four years, the Company has moved from a net debt position to a net cash surplus of ₹ 443 Crore at the end of FY26.
Free Cash Flow (FCF) increased to ₹ 237 Crore in FY26, representing a cash conversion ratio of 148% of PAT.

This growth was accompanied by sustained margin expansion, with adjusted EBITDA margin improving from 6.3% in FY23 to 12.2% in FY26, and robust cash generation resulting in a net cash surplus of ₹44,325.30 lakhs as of FY26, compared to a net debt position of ₹3,142.41 lakhs in FY23.
